title: Beckham leaves for Real Madrid
detail: Months after the boot incident with Ferguson (February 2003). £17.25m (transfers.csv).
evidence: The transfer to Real Madrid was announced in mid-June and formally completed on 1 July 2003, making Beckham the third Englishman to play for the club, after Laurie Cunningham and Steve McManaman, the latter of whom he succeeded in his position.

title: Ronaldo plays against United
detail: Sporting 3–1 United; Ferguson decides to sign him. United's season page dates the friendly 7 August (friendlies.csv).
evidence: After Sporting defeated Manchester United 3–1 in a friendly on 6 August 2003, United manager Alex Ferguson was determined to acquire Ronaldo, describing him as "one of the most exciting young players" he had ever seen.

title: Jimmy Davis dies
detail: The forward, on loan at Watford, dies in a car crash (date from the season page's transfer table).
evidence: Two days later, English forward Jimmy Davis died in a car crash.

Cristiano Ronaldo signs, takes the No. 7
evidence: Although he requested the number 28, his number at Sporting, he received the squad number 7 shirt, which had previously been worn by such United players as George Best, Eric Cantona and David Beckham.

title: Ronaldo's debut
evidence: His performance earned praise from Best, who hailed it as "undoubtedly the most exciting debut" he had ever seen.

The Battle of Old Trafford
detail: 0–0 with Arsenal; Van Nistelrooy at the centre of it.
evidence: In the 0–0 draw on 21 September 2003, later dubbed the Battle of Old Trafford, Van Nistelrooy was at the centre of one of the most infamous incidents of the Arsenal–Manchester United rivalry.

title: Rio Ferdinand misses a drugs test
evidence: In September 2003, he failed to attend a drug test scheduled to take place at United's Carrington training ground.

title: Ferguson touchline ban
detail: Two matches and £10,000 for abusing fourth official Jeff Winter.
evidence: 20 October 2003 – Two-match touchline ban and fined £10,000 after using abusive and/or insulting words towards fourth official Jeff Winter.

title: Ferguson v Magnier: Rock of Gibraltar
detail: The manager sues the club's major shareholder over a racehorse's stud rights.
evidence: In 2003, Ferguson launched legal action against the then major Manchester United shareholder John Magnier over stud rights for race horse Rock of Gibraltar.

title: Ferdinand banned for eight months
detail: From January 2004: misses the rest of the season, the FA Cup final and Euro 2004.
evidence: The Football Association (FA) Disciplinary Committee, chaired by Barry Bright, imposed an eight-month ban from January 2004 at club and international level and a £50,000 fine, meaning he would miss the rest of the season and some of the next along with all of Euro 2004.

title: The title slips away
detail: United are 1st after 19 rounds and 7th over the second half of the season (see summary.json).
evidence: However, the club surrendered the Premier League title to unbeaten champions Arsenal, with a second-half dip in league form coinciding with Rio Ferdinand starting an eight-month ban from football due to a missed drugs test and restricting United to a third-place finish.

title: Louis Saha signs
evidence: Arriving in the winter transfer window was Louis Saha, who signed from Fulham on 23 January for a fee of £12.82 million.

evidence: He scored his 100th goal for the club in a dramatic 4–3 victory over Everton on 7 February 2004.
